title: Spotlight on UN desertification summit as it mulls how to spend $12bn war chest

paragraphs.en: As swathes of the northern hemisphere bake in what could be the hottest year on record, with wildfires blazing across North America and Europe and heatwaves afflicting millions across Asia, the UN’s bi-annual talks on desertification have assumed much greater importance – and have started attracting more money.
paragraphs.zh: 随着北半球大片地区在可能是创纪录最热的一年中饱受炙烤，野火在北美和欧洲多地肆虐，热浪影响亚洲数百万民众，联合国每两年一次的防治荒漠化谈判已变得重要得多——也开始吸引更多资金。

paragraphs.en: Work will begin this week on allocating more than $12bn (£8.9bn) to vulnerable countries to help them deal with drought and land degradation, when scores of countries gather in Mongolia for Cop17.
paragraphs.zh: 本周，数十个国家将齐聚蒙古国参加Cop17会议，开始着手将超过120亿美元（合89亿英镑）的资金分配给脆弱国家，帮助它们应对干旱和土地退化问题。

paragraphs.en: Yasmine Fouad, executive secretary of the UN Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD), whose 17th “conference of the parties” begins in Ulaanbaatar on 17 August, said the negotiations would “send a positive signal of multilateralism”.
paragraphs.zh: 《联合国防治荒漠化公约》（UNCCD）执行秘书亚斯敏·福阿德表示，这次谈判将“发出多边主义的积极信号”。该公约第17次“缔约方会议”将于8月17日在乌兰巴托开幕。

paragraphs.en: The key aim is to put pledges of billions of dollars made two years ago into action through projects in the developing world.
paragraphs.zh: 核心目标是将两年前做出的数十亿美元认捐承诺，通过发展中国家的发展项目落到实处。

paragraphs.en: Countries around the world are bracing for food price rises as a result of damage to harvests from record heat and lack of water, and the World Food Programme predicts that 50 million more people could be pushed into hunger by the “ super El Niño ” weather system currently developing. Initiatives to restore land and prevent drought have up to now been poorly funded and badly managed.
paragraphs.zh: 世界各国的农民正因创纪录的高温和缺水对收成造成的破坏，面临食品价格上涨的预期。世界粮食计划署预测，目前正在发展的“超级厄尔尼诺”天气系统可能再使5000万人陷入饥饿。迄今为止，旨在恢复土地、预防干旱的举措一直资金不足、管理不善。

paragraphs.en: According to Fouad, that situation was changing rapidly as nations began to recognise the risk. “At the heart of our discussion is the topic of food security,” she said. “The more you work on restoring land, the more you have productive soil to ensure food security. That kind of narrative should be part of our finance [initiatives].”
paragraphs.zh: 据福阿德介绍，随着各国开始认识到这一风险，这种情况正在迅速改变。“我们讨论的核心议题是粮食安全。”她说，“你越是致力于恢复土地，就越能拥有肥沃的土壤来保障粮食安全。这种理念应当成为我们融资（计划）的一部分。”

paragraphs.en: The UNCCD was signed in 1992, one of a trio of environmental treaties launched at the Earth summit in Rio de Janeiro, alongside the better known UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), which is parent treaty to the Paris agreement of 2015; and the Convention on Biological Diversity, which includes targets on protecting species. Over the last three decades, the desertification treaty has been the “poor relation”, garnering the least attention of the three and producing scant progress.
paragraphs.zh: 《联合国防治荒漠化公约》于1992年签署，是在里约热内卢地球峰会上推出的三项环境条约之一，另外两项分别是更广为人知的《联合国气候变化框架公约》（UNFCCC）——它是2015年《巴黎协定》的母条约——以及包含保护物种目标的《生物多样性公约》。在过去三十年里，防治荒漠化条约一直是“穷亲戚”，在三个条约中获得的关注最少，进展也寥寥无几。

paragraphs.en: But that is changing. Saudi Arabia – a petrostate that for years has blocked action on greenhouse gas emissions and any mention of fossil fuels at UNFCCC meetings , and has refused calls to provide climate finance – is an enthusiastic backer of UNCCD . The kingdom, which hosted the Cop16 UNCCD summit in 2024, has pledged hundreds of millions of dollars to its aims, as well as joining with allies through larger groups and institutions to offer much bigger collective pledges.
paragraphs.zh: 但情况正在改变。沙特阿拉伯——这个多年来一直在UNFCCC会议上阻挠温室气体减排行动和对化石燃料的任何提及、并拒绝提供气候融资的石油国家——却是UNCCD的热心支持者。这个曾在2024年主办UNCCD第十六次缔约方会议的王国，已承诺为其目标投入数亿美元，并与盟友一道，通过更大的团体和机构提出了数额大得多的集体认捐。
